repairs.before: When Hao was about to conduct a northern expedition, Xizhi thought it would certainly fail, and with a letter stopped him; the words were very urgent and thorough.
repairs.after: When Hao was about to conduct a northern expedition, Xizhi thought it would certainly fail, and tried to stop him with a letter; the words were very urgent and thorough.
repairs.sourceBasedReason: 以書止之 states an attempt to dissuade through a letter. The next sentence says 浩遂行, so the English claim that the letter stopped him incorrectly asserts success. The idiomatic field already says urging him to desist and is accurate.
repairs.pairedFieldChecked: When Yin Hao prepared a northern campaign, Wang Xizhi was convinced it would end in disaster and sent him a letter urging him to desist, in the frankest terms.

repairs.before: Huan Wen was at odds with Yin Hao when Wang Xizhi wrote against the northern campaign
repairs.after: Huan Wen was at odds with Yin Hao when Wang Xizhi wrote to urge concord between court and frontier.
repairs.sourceBasedReason: s0035 records the concord admonition prompted by discord. s0036 separately introduces the northern-campaign warning with 及浩將北伐. The current glossary event conflates the two letters. This non-date event-text correction needs the editorial/source route, not a date-only repair.

sourceUnits.zh: 羲之既拜護軍，又苦求宣城郡，不許，乃以為右軍將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: After Xizhi had accepted Guarding the Army, he also bitterly sought Xuancheng commandery; it was not permitted, and so he was made General of the Right Army and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi did accept the post of General Who Guards the Army, then pleaded repeatedly for Xuancheng commandery. When that was denied, he was appointed General of the Right Army and internal administrator of Kuaiji.

sourceUnits.zh: 時殷浩與桓溫不協，羲之以國家之安在於內外和，因以與浩書以戒之，浩不從。

translations.literal: At the time Yin Hao and Huan Wen were not harmonious; Xizhi took the state's security as lying in inner and outer harmony, and therefore wrote to Hao to warn him; Hao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao and Huan Wen were at odds. Wang Xizhi believed the realm could be secure only if court and frontier remained at peace, so he wrote to admonish Yin Hao, who paid no heed.

sourceUnits.zh: 及浩將北伐，羲之以為必敗，以書止之，言甚切至。

translations.literal: When Hao was about to conduct a northern expedition, Xizhi thought it would certainly fail, and with a letter stopped him; the words were very urgent and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Hao prepared a northern campaign, Wang Xizhi was convinced it would end in disaster and sent him a letter urging him to desist, in the frankest terms.

translations.literal: Hao then proceeded and indeed was defeated by Yao Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao went ahead anyway and was routed by Yao Xiang.

translations.literal: Again planning a second undertaking, he again sent Hao a letter saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Yin plotted a second offensive, Wang Xizhi wrote to him again:
